title: Jason Cohen: Bootstrapping SmartBear vs raising $250M for WP Engine, and founder decision-making
summary: Jason Cohen explains why there is no single blueprint after building SmartBear (bootstrapped) and WP Engine (VC-backed). He covers raising only what ARR justifies, how to think about AI as a founder, why customer outcomes should drive strategy, and how to make big life decisions by widening options.

principles.text: Raise no more than your ARR, at a valuation you can grow into, so the next round stays possible.
principles.quote: I never wanted to raise more money than the amount of ARR we had. Get that way we're not We're have enough money to do something that's appropriate to our size, but not so much that you know, sometimes you drown in that.

principles.text: Most businesses aren't venture-sized, and that is fine; VC funds very few successful companies.
principles.quote: Most things aren't, and that's not saying anything bad. Most of my companies weren't, and that's not saying anything bad about them. Just most products aren't going to make billions in revenue or be worth tens billions.

principles.text: AI predictions without a timeline are useless; instead build around customers' unchanged problems solved in new ways.
principles.quote: the customer have the same problems they always had

principles.text: Aim your vision at the customer's ultimate success metric (revenue, clean audit), even if you can't measure it directly; ask customers whether you are delivering it.
principles.quote: the best way for any company to think about it is how do you make your customers successful in the way that they measure it? Best is revenue.

principles.text: Expand new bets from adjacent strengths: existing distribution and data make new products a better bet. In AI, distribution is easier than building something that works.
principles.quote: it still needs to be adjacent, which means leveraging some of the things I just said, where it's like, "Well, if we built this at our current customers would want it." So the distribution channel would be in.

principles.text: Pick strategies that use your strengths, with weaknesses either irrelevant or seen as strengths by your target market.
principles.quote: understand your strengths, your weaknesses, the capabilities and assets that you have and then ask, "Can I do a project or startup where the the startup strategy is that it will succeed if the things that you're strong in are used?
